A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original language-model pretraining experiments, synthetic-data experiments, emergence-point regressions, and supplementary analyses using several induction-head metrics.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds training-seed replications, predictive modeling, validation-loss analyses, and corpus/tokenizer data analyses.

M1.justification: V3 Section 7.3 adds a sigmoid predictor of prefix-matching score from log frequency and log reliability, with an explicit decision boundary. This supplements the retained emergence-time law; the language-model architectures and substantive constrained-generation procedure remain the same.

E1.justification: Appendix L substantially expands direct corpus-statistics coverage beyond CC100 to FineWeb, Dolma, and The Pile, including web and mixed-domain data. All four corpora are analyzed with three tokenizers. This is additional data-analysis coverage; induction-head training experiments are not replicated across these combinations.

E2.justification: The full and model-size-free emergence regressions remain compared in Table 5. No external baseline method is added or removed. The additional tokenizers are settings for corpus analysis, rather than competing methods evaluated against a proposed tokenizer.

E3.justification: V3 adds final-loss evaluation with identical 64-token validation chunks and a batch-128 context sweep extending to 4096. The semi-natural grid grows from 50 to 60 configurations through reliability 0.2, and repetitive-chunk proportions extend to 80–100%. Displayed PS and AR normalizers also change; the PDFs do not establish whether retained scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: V3 adds quantitative onset/slope analyses in Figure 2, seed robustness in Section 6.2, emergence-versus-validation-loss analysis in Section 9, and corpus/tokenizer sensitivity analysis in Appendix L. These address additional questions about repeatability, training outcomes, and generalization. V2's alternative-metric analyses are retained in Appendix K.

E5.justification: V2 already reports regression uncertainty and five-fold cross-validation. V3 explicitly trains two additional seeds for six configurations, reporting three-seed confidence intervals and standard deviations in Figure 4 and Table 6. It also adds onset/slope correlation tests and sequence-level standard-deviation reporting for the corpus analysis.

E6.justification: New results include reliability-0.2 heatmap cells, a boundary-fit MSE of 0.019, three-seed estimates, and corpus/tokenizer statistics in Table 8. Section 9 newly reports validation loss decreasing until batch size 64 and then increasing with context fixed at 1024. The original regression and cross-validation values in Tables 3–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1), (3), and (4) change normalization from 1/(|x|-1) to 1/|x|. Appendix H corrects the stated KL expression from a ratio of logarithms to the logarithm of a probability ratio. Section 7.3 also derives an explicit fitted boundary. Existing entropy derivations remain, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central emergence-time and repetition claims remain. V3 adds an introduction/conclusion claim connecting emergence timing non-monotonically to final validation loss and training efficiency. It narrows categoriality/distribution claims to modulation near the decision boundary and qualifies the conclusion about individual properties by the PS metric.

C2.justification: V3 adds critical-batch-size and retrieval-difficulty explanations, explicitly suggesting that the predictive law may describe only a pre-saturation regime while acknowledging uncertainty about large-context reversals. Appendix G questions the naturalness of uniform token-level repetition constraints, and Appendix L qualifies its corpus comparisons as proxies. Appendix C also corrects the earlier reversed interpretation of negative regression coefficients.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from predict-ih-review to predict-ih. Appendix L documents tokenizer vocabulary sizes and an analysis sample exceeding 10M tokens. Core training hyperparameters remain in Table 2; the 64-token synthetic training context was already disclosed in v2 Appendix E.

R1.justification: V3 adds critical-batch-size references by McCandlish and Merrill, plus references for the additional corpora and tokenizers, and removes Oh and Schuler (2023). Its comparison with Zucchet et al. shifts toward competing context-size effects. The broader positioning within induction-head and in-context-learning research remains intact.

P1.justification: The predictive-law exposition is condensed and separated from Experiment 1 into a dedicated Predictability and Robustness section. Results and discussion are substantially rewritten around shifting, slanting, and training dynamics, alongside widespread terminology and grammar editing. Appendix headings are reorganized while their existing technical material is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains onset/slope panels, and the repetition heatmap becomes an expanded observed-versus-predicted display. V3 adds seed, validation-loss, and corpus/tokenizer figures and tables. Regression tables gain significance coloring and are relocated. Figure 11 explicitly redisplays Figure 7 rather than contributing another experiment.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens support for its predictions: v2's single-seed timing results gain direct repeatability checks for six configurations, and its visually characterized repetition boundary gains an explicit quantitative fit. Controlled validation-loss analysis and candid discussion of possible saturation limits improve practical interpretation, while formula corrections improve mathematical correctness. Corpus generalization remains a proxy analysis and causal explanations remain tentative, but these limits are acknowledged and the overall gains are substantial.
